title: I built a card game where you fuse creatures and AI generates the result - millions of possible combinations. Workflow and models in description.
author: VirtualJamesHarrison
selftext:
**Fuse creatures to power up your team or weaken enemies.** Every combination creates a unique AI-generated hybrid based on parent types and traits - compatible elements synergize for stronger stats, while the AI blends visual features from both parents into completely new art.

**Build with:** **ai-studio** to prototype, **Gemini 3 Flash** for front end and **Opus 4.5** for backend/game logic.

**Models**: Game logic with **gemini-3-flash-preview** and images with **flux-schnell**. As much as I love nano banana its just too dam expensive.

Play now for free at [https://chimeracraft.app/](https://chimeracraft.app/)

comments.author: Touitoui
comments.body:
The game is starting nicely!  
  
Few issues though:  
\-First run, no fusion worked ("please try again", with EVERY cards)  
\-The next two runs, I sometimes had the same error with already fused card, but I'm not sure if it was an error like before, or if the fusion couldn't work with those creatures (A different message would be nice if it wasn't a system error)  
\-Fusion takes way too long (around 5-10 seconds for me), maybe letting us play while the image get generated could ease it up if you intend to keep flux? (The fusion worked, the monster is usable, but you get a blank image until it's generated)  
\-Alchemy points are useful at first (1 card first turn, 2 action on the second, etc...) but feel useless once your hand is empty for the first time  
\-Didn't feel any difference between easy and medium difficulty (work in progress?)  
\-An option to change your username would be nice (I connected with Google, my full name is displayed on every new cards)  
\-An option to go back to the main menu would be usefull  
\-Overall, the gameplay currently lacks... something. You place your cards, try a fusion, wait for a fusion to finish, do another fusion, wait, ignore the enemy killing itself on your OP creatures, repeat until you're tired of drawing one card at a time, then waste the enemy's life in one/two turns.

The game will become something real nice once the gameplay loop get balanced a little more!  
  
As for the "Fusion takes way too long", maybe check with u/gangstarob7 ?   
Their game [https://infinite-card.net/](https://infinite-card.net/) use a similar system to yours (Game logic + descriptions handled by a LLM and image generated based on it's description), we're currently testing flux (Not everyone like to wait 5s for the image, but the cards are usable while you wait, making it "not that much of an issue". And we may switch back to a faster model).

Anyway, keep up the good work!

replies.author: GangstaRob7
replies.body: Maybe OP and I could team up to make a game, making a game like this by yourself can be tough ... Either way we are moving towards more and more complex AI games, which was my goal when making Infinite Card, impressive how you were able to make this so quickly

replies.author: VirtualJamesHarrison
replies.body:
Thanks for the awesome feedback,  the errors should be fixed i had a deploy error. 

Seem is something i am playing with, I want the cards to look like that fit the mutation so this takes a bit more time as the prompt is fairly large and complex. But everything is cached so once a discovery is made it should be fairly quick for future players.   But this version is using flux-schnell. 

I agree with the fact the game is overly simple, my thinking is adding passive abilities to certain creatures, that can allow for more complex combos and such, but need to think on this.

replies.author: Touitoui
replies.body:
(I played around a little more...)

  
If by mutation points you mean how many time you can mutate in a round, it's the alchemy points at the top of the screen.   
If you mean the max time a creature can be mutated, you'll have to look at their level, visible when you hover their names. Max lvl 10, so fusing a lvl 6 and a lvl 5 will fail (11), but a lvl 6 and a lvl 4 will give you a lvl 10.  
You can fuse a card already in play, but the "source" need to be able to attack (not exhausted / zzz), and it will exhaust the destination (if it's not already the case).

comments.author: KefkeWren
comments.body:
Interesting concept, but the computer opponent never tries to fuse, and since the only options are "Fuse" and "Attack", it's rather easy to steamroll. Especially since; 1) you can attack before fusing, and 2) you don't have to attack your opponent’s creatures. 

Trying to weaken the opponent feels pointless since, first of all they never have anything but basic creatures in the first place, and secondly it seems to use the same logic as fusing your own, so it will only make them stronger.

Also, the element system doesn't seem to come into play at all.
